Forward Deployed Software Engineers (FDSEs) work directly with customers to quickly understand their greatest problems and design and implement solutions to use data against them. Our customers rely on Palantir’s platforms for some of their most critical operations, and projects often start with an open ended question like "How do we evaluate wildfire risk and optimize a power grid as a result" or "How do we quickly assess our food supply chain and modify it to deliver life saving assistance on time?" Wego Chemical Group is a global distributor and sourcing partner of chemicals and ingredients. Job Summary
The AI and Workflow Engineer is responsible for finding, building, and running AI automation across Wego's business processes. Working in a forward-deployed model, this role sits with business teams to identify the workflows and processes AI can automate, then designs and delivers solutions using Claude, Microsoft Power Automate / Power Platform, and Microsoft Copilot. Build and consume REST APIs and webhooks to integrate AI solutions with Oracle ERP, Oracle OTM, Salesforce, SAP Concur, and other business applications.
Develop Claude skills, connectors (MCP servers), Cowork tasks, and scheduled tasks for repeatable business workflows.

Develop applications on the Claude API with structured JSON outputs, using Claude Code as a core development tool.
Write and maintain Python or JavaScript services, scripts, and user interfaces, using Git for source control and code reviews.
Work with SQL, vector, and graph databases to prepare, store, and retrieve data for AI solutions.
Build testing, evaluation, and prompt engineering into every solution to prove accurate output before and after go-live.
Monitor token usage, cost per run, and model selection to keep solutions cost-effective.
Apply security and governance controls, including least-privilege access, secrets handling, skill vetting, and human approval checkpoints.
Work closely with the Enterprise Applications and IT Operations teams on integrations, system changes, and ongoing support.
Document designs, procedures, and controls, and train business users on new solutions.
Track emerging AI technologies and best practices and share recommendations with IT and business leaders.
Key Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, software engineering, information technology, data science, artificial intelligence, or a related field preferred; equivalent hands-on experience will be considered in place of a degree.
2–4 years of hands-on experience building automation, integration, or AI solutions for business users.
Track record of shipping AI solutions into production that business users run day to day.
Proficiency in Python or JavaScript; working knowledge of HTML and CSS.
Strong SQL skills and experience with vector and graph databases.
Hands-on experience building and consuming REST APIs and webhooks.
Experience building with large language models and generative AI, preferably Claude (Claude API, skills, MCP, Claude Code, Agent SDK).
Experience with Microsoft Power Automate / Power Platform and Microsoft Copilot.
Understanding of LLM token cost, model selection, and cost optimization.
Solid software development fundamentals, including testing, debugging, Git version control, and object-oriented programming.
Knowledge of security practices for AI and integrations, including least privilege, secrets management, and human-in-the-loop approval.
Experience integrating with ERP or CRM platforms such as Oracle ERP Cloud, Oracle OTM, Salesforce, or SAP Concur preferred.
Familiarity with cloud platforms (Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud) preferred.
Strong business sense, with the ability to turn a process problem into a practical automation and explain it to non-technical users.
Excellent communication skills; self-directed, works well independently and within a team, and is open about skill gaps and how to close them.
Location & Work Arrangement
Great Neck, NY (Wego headquarters). Remote work will be considered for a candidate with an excellent fit who is willing to travel to headquarters on an agreed frequency.

reason: Stack +31; Title fit +6; Exp fit +10; US +10
description_preview:
About Us:
At ClarityPay, we’re redefining the point-of-sale credit market to bring more value to merchants. Based in NYC and Atlanta, our fast-growing fintech empowers large merchants with configurable “Pay-Over-Time” tools— including monthly installments, BNPL, and revolving products. We solve complex credit challenges with speed, precision, and intelligence.
Our values guide everything we do: we put merchants first, stay data-driven, always know the why, learn relentlessly, and win together as a team.
Role Overview:
ClarityPay is seeking Forward Deployed Engineers to embed with the teams that run the company and turn how they work into dependable, AI-native systems. You will sit with process owners in finance, credit and portfolio risk, servicing and collections, and operations; scope the problem with them before building; ship agents, controls and automations into production; and stay through adoption as the named secondary owner of the process. You will join the Data & AI organization, working alongside engineers in New York and India on a shared platform, and alongside Product and Engineering you will build external-facing AI solutions for merchants and partners on the ClarityPay platform. You will use AI tooling to make the build the easy part, and you will be measured on what is adopted and relied upon, not on what is demoed.
Key Responsibilities:
Embed with process owners to map how the work actually runs, scope the problem with them before building, and agree success criteria and a baseline up front.
Own delivery end to end — discovery, technical scoping, system design, build and production rollout — and stay through adoption as the named secondary owner of the process.
Choose the simplest dependable solution: simplify or remove a step before automating it, then pick a scheduled job, a triggered job, or a bounded agent with a defined mandate, action set, escalation owner and pause conditions.
Write evaluations for everything you ship: prove the output is correct before a team depends on it, and re-check it as models, data and processes change.
Instrument what you build, and the processes around it, with detective (“day-zero”) controls — thresholds, exception inventories and alerting, each with an action path and a named owner — so a breach surfaces the same day, not at month-end.
Build external-facing AI solutions for merchants and partners with Product and Engineering; anything external ships through Engineering’s review and deployment standards.
Codify reusable patterns, evals and harness standards so the second deployment is faster than the first; prefer reusable capabilities over one agent per task, and bring field signal back to the platform roadmap.
Work inside ClarityPay’s controls for AI — evaluate before exposure, bound the exposure, keep a person at the gate — and propose where a human must review, where automation may act unattended, and what gets logged.
Own the value case: set impact hypotheses and baselines, measure before and after, and report to executives on business impact, total effort saved (including review and maintenance), control quality and reuse.
Continually promote and apply ClarityPay values; be a role model of trust and integrity.
What Success Looks Like in Your First 6–12 Months:
Desktop and spreadsheet-based reporting processes are inventoried, baselined and moved onto AI agentic systems running on governed data, with a person at the gate where judgment is needed.
Recurring performance reporting — portfolio, collections, servicing and finance — is produced by agents from governed metrics rather than manual pulls, on time and traceable to source.
Day-zero controls are live in your first processes, each with a threshold, an action path and a named owner, so breaches surface the same day.
The effort returned is measured against the baseline, net of review, exceptions and maintenance, and reported to executives.
At least one external-facing solution for merchants or partners is in production and adopted.
The patterns, evals and agent-harness standards you built are reused by the next deployment.
Qualifications:
Curious, energetic, positive, solution-oriented, collaborative, trusted.
2–5 years of software engineering or technical deployment experience that includes working directly with business users — in operations, business systems, solutions engineering, or technical consulting.
Production experience with LLMs: prompt engineering, agent or skill development, and evaluation. Things other people depend on, not demos.
Strong Python and SQL: you write and review production code and use AI-assisted development to move faster. Low-code and automation platforms (e.g., Retool, Zapier, n8n) are useful, not a substitute.
Data fluency in a lakehouse environment (e.g., Databricks, ClickHouse): pull answers out of governed data, build reliable pipelines, and catch when the output is wrong.
High agency and comfort with ambiguity — you will choose what to automate as often as you are told.
Strong discovery and communication skills: able to sit with a collections specialist or a finance analyst, understand their workflow, and explain trade-offs to a non-technical audience; comfortable working across time zones with engineering colleagues in India.
Judgment about what should not be automated — where the cost of being wrong outweighs the time saved.
Nice to Have:
Fintech, lending, payments, banking, or another regulated environment.
Experience building MCP servers, sub-agents, or agent skills.
MLOps or experimentation experience: evaluation frameworks, staged A/B tests, model monitoring.
Prior forward-deployed, professional services, or founding-engineer experience.
How You’ll Know This Role Is Right for You:
You see manual, repetitive work and cannot leave it alone.
You would rather ship a working automation this week than design the perfect one this quarter.
You have receipts — things you actually built that other people now depend on.

About Us
Mintive helps companies put agents to work safely. We exist to help companies do more of their work with agents, and we build the infrastructure that makes a company's own work runnable by them. That has to start from trust. Our first product is an MCP gateway that gives those agents governed access to company data and tools.
Before agents can touch Slack, GitHub, Jira, Snowflake, internal databases, or production systems, you need to know what they can reach, what they did, and why they were allowed to do it. Most people carry far more permissions than any single task needs. If an agent uses your token directly, it inherits all of them. Our gateway product scopes that access down to exactly what an agent needs to do its job and captures the data flows and audit logs security teams need. From there we are building the rest of the agent stack: connectors, monitoring, sandboxing, long-running agents, and memory, with the goal of becoming the system a company's work runs on.
We work in person in the San Francisco Bay Area. The structure is flat and the market moves fast, so you have a lot of latitude over what you work on and how.
We are AI-native. Everyone uses Claude and Codex every day, and we have more agents than employees. They run in Slack alongside the team and handle sales, marketing, deal ops, and engineering on the same gateway we sell to customers, and we are building an entire company operating system around them.
Since launching in February 2026, we have grown to 50+ paying customers, with strong inbound demand. Customers include Coursera, Arlo, and Braze. We are backed by Cowboy Ventures and Coatue, with angels including Frederic Kerrest (Okta), Michael Grinich (WorkOS), Andrej Karpathy, Jeff Dean, and Scott Belsky. Our founders are machine learning experts from Stanford, Berkeley, and CMU, with applied research at Google Brain and Waymo, and one co-founded Coursera.
The Job
You will own features end to end, from conception to production, across our gateway infrastructure, enterprise deployments, and agentic systems. The work leans backend and infra, but nothing is off limits: when the product needs a better UI you build it, and when a connector breaks during a security review you fix it.
Claude and Codex are your primary working environment, and you use a fleet of agents to move faster than a team this size has any right to. Agents write much of the code and review PRs, so your real job is the judgment they cannot make: shaping the problem, making architecture, product, and UX calls, hardening enterprise paths, designing connectors, protecting security-sensitive surfaces, and catching generated code that is quietly wrong. Roles are blurred and we ship within hours, and you will learn directly from the founders and from customers.
We hire across levels, from strong early-career builders to seasoned engineers, and we set level and pay to match. What matters most is judgment, range, and how fast you ship.
About You
You are a builder with a track record of shipping to real users, whether that is a product, an internal tool, an open-source project, or a serious side project. You ship, then iterate, without waiting for specs or approvals.
You have strong fundamentals and learn fast. How quickly you pick things up matters as much as years of experience.
You care about product value and customer needs over technical purity.
You take infra seriously. You think about blast radius, trust boundaries, and what happens when your code is in the path of every customer's agents.
You can read unfamiliar code, reason from first principles, and explain your tradeoffs.
You are comfortable across the stack (TypeScript, Python, CockroachDB), or you pick up new languages, protocols, and domains fast.
You are excited to build with agents, and to learn when they help and when they hide a problem.

Background in security, identity, or permission systems.
Contributions to open source, MCP servers, or agentic frameworks.
Design sensibility: engineers who care about design, designers who think about infrastructure.

description_preview:
About Destro AI
Destro AI is building the intelligence layer for robotics — the system that coordinates robots, humans, and workflows across complex real-world operations. Founded by former leaders from HAI Robotics, Dexterity, and Matic, Destro is built on a simple thesis: robotics has solved movement, but not decision-making. Destro is backed by investors who have previously invested in and built companies like Brex, Figma, Notion, and Instacart.
Destro's MothershipOS is a shared brain across all robots, unlocking complex factory and warehouse workflows. Unlike traditional systems that rely on local intelligence on each robot, Destro brings global intelligence across the entire operation. Destro recently closed its Seed round at one of the highest valuations for a robotics company at this stage, and is already deploying in production with large enterprise operators.
About The Role
We're hiring a Robotics Forward Deployed Engineer, to own the software that runs MothershipOS in live customer warehouses. This role is responsible for writing and maintaining production code, not solely for troubleshooting it, and will serve as the engineering presence on-site when systems need to be brought up, stabilized, or restored to full function.
Schedule Expectations
This is a field deployment role, not a standard office-hours position. Warehouse operations run multiple shifts, and go-lives, incidents, and integrations are not confined to business hours.
Regular work outside standard business hours should be expected, including nights and weekends. Go-lives are frequently scheduled during off-hours or weekend downtime windows to avoid disrupting customer operations.
This role may be paged for production issues, including robot faults, network outages, and server failures, outside normal hours, and is expected to respond promptly, either remotely or on-site.
Extensive travel to customer sites is required, at times on short notice.
Candidates seeking a fixed 9-to-5, Monday-through-Friday schedule are unlikely to find this role a fit.
What You'll Do
Software
Write, test, and maintain the software services that run MothershipOS at customer sites, including deployment tooling and diagnostic utilities.
Design and build internal tools that make field deployments faster and more repeatable.
Translate field learnings into production-hardening fixes and improvements in the core codebase.
Maintain clear technical documentation and runbooks so issues can be diagnosed consistently across sites.
Field Deployment
Deploy and validate Destro's software stack in live warehouses, working directly with customer operations, IT, and engineering teams.
Own production issues end-to-end during launch and stabilization, including off-hours incidents.
Improve uptime, throughput, and reliability of deployed systems through both code and infrastructure changes.
Systems and Infrastructure
Build and maintain containerized services (Docker Compose) running on Destro-managed servers and edge devices.
Work with cloud infrastructure (GCP) for image management, versioning, and deployment tooling.
Configure and troubleshoot networking, including VLANs, DHCP, internal DNS, and certificate-based service security.
Debug across the full stack: robot state faults, sensor issues, API failures, container networking, database queries, and monitoring dashboards.
Who You Are
2 to 6 years of experience in systems engineering, robotics software, backend engineering, infrastructure, or field engineering, with genuine software development experience rather than field support alone.
Comfortable being paged off-hours and traveling on short notice.
Able to operate independently in ambiguous, high-pressure environments without a fully specified solution.
Calm under pressure, direct with customers, and demonstrates strong ownership.
Technical Skills
Required
Strong Python or C++, with the ability to write maintainable, production-grade code.
Hands-on Docker/Docker Compose experience, including building, deploying, debugging, and versioning images.
Linux/server administration: command line, logs, processes, systemd, firewalls.
Networking fundamentals: DHCP, DNS, VLANs, static IP reservations, TLS/certificates.
Experience with APIs and communication protocols (REST, WebSockets, MQTT).
Proficiency with Git and standard software development workflows.
Strongly Preferred
Experience with AMRs, warehouse automation, or fleet management.
Cloud deployment experience, ideally GCP.
Familiarity with observability tooling such as Grafana, Prometheus, or time-series databases.
WMS/WES/ERP integration experience.
Nice to Have
Experience with robot task allocation, scheduling, or routing.
Experience with wearables, scanners, or other warehouse hardware.

description_preview:
Why USAA?
At USAA, our mission is to empower our members to achieve financial security through highly competitive products, exceptional service and trusted advice. We seek to be the #1 choice for the military community and their families.
Embrace a fulfilling career at USAA, where our core values – honesty, integrity, loyalty and service – define how we treat each other and our members. Be part of what truly makes us special and impactful.
We are proud to support active-duty military spouses. USAA roles may offer remote or hybrid flexibility for active-duty military spouses consistent with applicable policy and business needs.
The Opportunity
As a dedicated
Context Engineer
are you fascinated by the frontier of generative AI, LLMs, and autonomous agents? Do you bridge the gap between human intent and machine execution? We are looking for a forward-thinking
Context Engineer
to join our team—someone who doesn't just build with AI, but shapes how business context, data, and logic are structured to drive real-world impact. In this role, you will sit at the intersection of business strategy, data science, and engineering, acting as the architect of prompts, workflows, and agent behaviors. If you are passionate about rapidly iterating on AI solutions, optimizing model outputs, and ensuring safe, compliant agent control design in a fast-paced environment, we want you on our team.
What You Will Do
Collaborates closely with cross-functional business, data science, and engineering teams to translate complex business objectives into effective AI and agentic workflows.
Designs, tests, and optimizes prompt architectures, context windows, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines to maximize LLM performance and accuracy.
Engineers and monitors autonomous or semi-autonomous AI agents, participating in iterative solution design and continuous refinement.
Applies qualitative and quantitative evaluation frameworks to assess model behavior, hallucinations, latency, and overall output quality against business use cases.
Adheres to rigorous risk, safety, and agent control design standards to ensure ethical AI deployment, alignment, and compliance with regulatory standards
Synthesizes complex AI outputs and multi-modal data insights into clear, actionable recommendations and communication materials for peer review and stakeholder alignment.
Documents system instructions, prompt templates, agent logic, and testing frameworks comprehensively to facilitate transparent peer reviews and compliance audits.
Explores and rapidly adopts emerging generative AI technologies, frameworks, and tooling to continually enhance solution strategies.
Delivers findings and demonstrates agent capabilities in a manner that influences mid-level management, secures stakeholder buy-in, and accelerates AI adoption.
Ensures risks associated with AI operations, data leakage, and automated business activities are effectively identified, measured, monitored, and controlled.
What You Have
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Software Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical/quantitative field; OR 4 years of relevant education and/or technical experience.
2+ years of hands-on experience working with modern AI/ML technologies, data analytics, or software development—specifically involving LLM applications, prompt engineering, or workflow automation—OR an Advanced degree in Computer Science, AI, Data Science, or a related quantitative/technical discipline.
Demonstrated experience with Large Language Models (LLMs), prompt engineering patterns (e.g., Chain-of-Thought, few-shot), and working with major foundation model APIs or open-weights models.
Practical familiarity with AI orchestration frameworks and toolsets (e.g., LangChain, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, or custom agent frameworks) and vector databases.
Proficiency in Python and modern data manipulation tools, with the ability to query structured/unstructured data sources (SQL, APIs) to feed context into AI pipelines.
Solid understanding of AI risk management, guardrails, security best practices (e.g., mitigating prompt injection, data privacy), and agent control design.
Compensation range:
The salary range for this position is: $77,120 - $147,390
USAA does not provide visa sponsorship for this role. Please do not apply for this role if at any time (now or in the future) you will need immigration support (i.e., H-1B, TN, STEM OPT Training Plans, etc.).
Compensation:
USAA has an effective process for assessing market data and establishing ranges to ensure we remain competitive. You are paid within the salary range based on your experience and market data of the position. The actual salary for this role may vary by location.
Employees may be eligible for pay incentives based on overall corporate and individual performance and at the discretion of the USAA Board of Directors.
The above description reflects the details considered necessary to describe the principal functions of the job and should not be construed as a detailed description of all the work requirements that may be performed in the job.
Benefits:
At USAA our employees enjoy best-in-class benefits to support their physical, financial, and emotional wellness. These benefits include comprehensive medical, dental and vision plans, 401(k), pension, life insurance, parental benefits, adoption assistance, paid time off program with paid holidays plus 16 paid volunteer hours, and various wellness programs. Additionally, our career path planning and continuing education assists employees with their professional goals.
For more details on our outstanding benefits, visit our benefits page on USAAjobs.com.
Applications for this position are accepted on an ongoing basis, this posting will remain open until the position is filled. Thus, interested candidates are encouraged to apply the same day they view this posting.

Job Description
About Arize
AI is rapidly transforming the world. As generative AI reshapes industries, teams need powerful ways to monitor, troubleshoot, and optimize their AI systems. That’s where we come in. Arize AI is the leading AI & Agent Engineering observability and evaluation platform, empowering AI engineers to ship high-performing, reliable agents and applications. From first prototype to production scale, Arize AX unifies build, test, and run in a single workspace—so teams can ship faster with confidence.
We’re a Series C company backed by top-tier investors, with over $135M in funding and a rapidly growing customer base of 150+ leading enterprises and Fortune 500 companies. Customers like Booking.com, Uber, Siemens, and PepsiCo leverage Arize to deliver AI that works.
The Opportunity
We are seeking an experienced Forward Deployed AI Engineer to work directly with client engineering teams, manage multiple concurrent projects, and drive technical solutions that extend beyond our core platform offering. This is a client-facing, hands-on technical role that combines deep AI expertise with business acumen to deliver results on tight timelines while building lasting client relationships. While we are a remote-first company, the nature of this role requires candidates to be based in the San Francisco Bay area/PST time zone.
What You’ll Do
Partner directly with enterprise AI teams to design, implement, and scale production-grade GenAI observability and evaluation programs.
Lead technical discussions with customer stakeholders ranging from engineers to senior executives, translating business priorities into scalable technical solutions.
Build custom integrations, tooling, and workflows that extend the Arize platform to meet customer-specific requirements.
Manage multiple concurrent customer engagements, driving projects from scoping through delivery while maintaining a high bar for technical execution and customer experience.
Collaborate cross-functionally with Sales, CS, Product, and Engineering teams to shape implementation strategy, influence product direction, and expand customer impact.
Help define and scale best practices, technical playbooks, and delivery methodologies for the growing Forward Deployed Engineering team.
What We’re Looking For
Software Development: 2-5 years of hands-on software development experience with strong technical foundations. We work extensively in Python, Java, and TypeScript, and expect candidates to be comfortable working in at least two of those languages.
ML/AI Engineering: Experience building MLOps pipelines and/or developing, deploying, and iterating on Generative AI applications in production environments..
Cloud Technologies: Experience working with public cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, GCP, Azure) as well as containerization and orchestration technologies (e.g., Docker and Kubernetes).
Communication: Excellent communication skills with the ability to work effectively across both technical and business audiences. You should be comfortable engaging with senior executives on business outcomes and metrics, collaborating with engineers on technical implementation details, and translating seamlessly between the two.
Project Management: Proven ability to manage multiple client engineering engagements simultaneously and deliver high-quality technical outcomes under demanding timelines.
Adaptability: Comfortable operating in fast-paced startup or consulting environments, with the ability to navigate diverse client organizations, technical stacks, and evolving priorities.
Passion for AI: We live and breathe AI at Arize. The strongest candidates are genuinely excited about the space and energized by staying at the forefront of rapidly evolving AI technologies.
The estimated annual salary and variable compensation for this role is between $155,000 - $190,000, plus a competitive equity package. Actual compensation is determined based upon a variety of job related factors that may include: transferable work experience, skill sets, and qualifications. Total compensation also includes a comprehensive benefit package, including: medical, dental, vision, 401(k) plan, unlimited paid time off, generous parental leave plan, and others for mental and wellness support.
While we are a remote-first company, we have opened offices in New York City and the San Francisco Bay Area, as an option for those in those cities who wish to work in-person. For all other employees, there is a WFH monthly stipend to pay for co-working spaces.
More About Arize
Arize’s mission is to make the world’s AI work—and work for people.
Our founders came together through a shared frustration: while investments in AI are growing rapidly across every industry, organizations face a critical challenge—understanding whether AI is performing and how to improve it at scale.

Promaxo is rebuilding MRI around the point of care by transforming image-guided procedures with the world’s first portable, single-sided MRI platform. FDA-cleared, AI-powered, commercially deployed, and protected by more than 240 patents — the system installs in a small footprint without shielding and operates quietly to deliver improved patient experiences, outcomes and provider economics.

Practically, that means independent urology groups, ASCs and health systems are rebuilding their prostate care pathways right now - and we are in those rooms.
Position Summary
The Software Quality Engineer (SaMD) is a hands-on individual contributor supporting software quality engineering and product cybersecurity across Promaxo's
connected/software medical device products. This role executes software verification activities and
supports the FDA premarket cybersecurity documentation set - threat modeling, security architecture, security requirements, testing, labeling content, and postmarket vulnerability management - partnering closely with R&D/Software Engineering to embed security and quality requirements into the SDLC and QMS. This role operates under the oversight of the Senior Manager, Quality, Regulatory & Compliance.
Key Responsibilities
Software Quality & Verification
Execute software verification for connected device software and cloud-based components, translating requirements into test plans, test cases, and execution records.
Develop and maintain verification plans, protocols, and reports in compliance with FDA QMSR (21CFR 820), ISO 13485, and IEC 62304.
Support risk analysis, defect triage, and root-cause investigations for software issues.
Participate in design and code reviews, verifying design inputs and outputs meet regulatory and quality expectations.
Execute manual and automated testing spanning functional, integration, system, and regression testing.
Log, triage, and drive bugs/defects to resolution in Jira, coordinating with software engineering on root cause and fix verification.
Help establish test automation capability at Promaxo, building initial automated test frameworks to complement current manual testing processes and integrating them with CI/CD pipelines.
Product Cybersecurity Documentation
Support threat modeling (e.g., STRIDE-based methodology) and maintain the Security Risk Management File, including asset inventory, trust boundaries, and Software Bill of Materials (SBOM).
Support development of Security Architecture Views and the Security Requirements Specification across the FDA's eight security control categories.
Support security requirements verification, threat mitigation testing, vulnerability testing, and penetration testing, documenting results in the Cybersecurity Testing Report.
Support integration of ISO 14971 risk management and FDA cybersecurity guidance (aligned with AAMI TIR57) into SDLC and Design and Development File (DDF) documentation, including software requirements specifications, architecture/design documents, Risk Management Files, and traceability matrices.
Support postmarket cybersecurity surveillance, including monitoring for emerging vulnerabilities, coordinating vulnerability disclosures, and assessing the impact of security findings on product safety.
Support CAPA, complaints, and audit activities related to software and cybersecurity issues, contributing to root cause analysis and corrective actions.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
Work directly with R&D and Software Engineering to operationalize security and quality requirements throughout the product development lifecycle.
Support the Senior Manager, Quality, Regulatory & Compliance in preparing cybersecurity content for FDA submissions (e.g., 510(k)) and responding to review questions.
Escalate cybersecurity risk, testing, or documentation issues to the Senior Manager, Quality,
Regulatory & Compliance for review and sign-off.
Qualifications
3+ years of experience in software quality engineering or software testing within the medical device industry.
Working knowledge of IEC 62304 and ISO 14971; exposure to FDA premarket/postmarket cybersecurity guidance or AAMI TIR57 is a plus.
Experience with product cybersecurity testing and documentation, including threat modeling, security requirements specifications, SBOM, and vulnerability/penetration testing.
Experience with, or strong aptitude for, building test automation frameworks from the ground up (e.g., Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, PyTest, Selenium/Playwright, or similar), to help transition Promaxo's testing from manual to automated.
Proficiency with Jira (or similar issue-tracking tools) for bug logging, triage, and resolution tracking.
Comfortable working directly with software engineers to translate security and quality requirements into implementation.
Exposure to supporting FDA regulatory submissions (e.g., 510(k)) with cybersecurity or software documentation content is a plus.
Detail-oriented, with strong documentation skills suitable for regulated (FDA/QMS) environments.
Ability to safely work in and around magnetic-field MRI environments (i.e., no medically contraindicated implants or devices, per standard MRI safety screening).
Authorized to work in the United States.
Growth Path
This is an individual contributor role with direct exposure to FDA premarket cybersecurity submissions and medical device software quality engineering. It offers a pathway toward a Senior Quality Engineer or Cybersecurity Enginee

We require people to be on-site, 4 days/week at our Denver or NYC office and are unable to offer relocation support.
LG Ad Solutions
LG Ad Solutions is a global leader in connected TV (CTV) and cross-screen advertising. We pride ourselves on delivering state-of-the-art advertising solutions that integrate seamlessly with today's ever-evolving digital media landscape.
The Opportunity
We're growing our infrastructure team in Denver and looking for an engineer who has gotten their hands dirty with both physical infrastructure and cloud environments — someone who's moved past tutorials and has real scars from production systems. You don't need to have all the answers yet, but you should be able to own a task end-to-end, ask good questions, and learn fast in a hybrid environment that spans data centers and AWS.
You'll work alongside senior engineers on a team that's actively building out our on-premises layer — provisioning servers, managing network infrastructure, extending our IaC practices, and keeping everything running reliably. This is a role where you'll be doing real work from day one, with mentorship and context from engineers who've built these systems before.
A Note On What We're Not Looking For
This role isn't for someone who's only worked in fully managed cloud environments and wants to stay there. The on-prem side of this team is real and growing — if physical infrastructure sounds boring or intimidating, this probably isn't the right fit. If it sounds interesting and you want to learn it properly, we'd love to talk.
Responsibilities
Hybrid Infrastructure
Assist with deployment and maintenance of on-premises compute, storage, and networking infrastructure alongside our AWS environment
Participate in bare metal server provisioning and OS deployment workflows
Support day-to-day network operations: troubleshoot connectivity issues, help maintain firewall rules, VLANs, and VPN configurations under senior guidance
Help maintain and document storage systems and cloud connectivity configurations
Automation & Platform Support
Write and maintain Infrastructure as Code using Terraform and Ansible for both on-prem and cloud resources
Support CI/CD pipeline maintenance and help onboard teams to existing platform tooling
Assist with Kubernetes cluster operations — deployments, troubleshooting, resource management — across bare metal and EKS environments
Contribute automation scripts and tooling improvements in Python or Bash
Security & Reliability
Follow established security standards for on-prem and cloud: help maintain RBAC configurations, apply patches, and support access management processes
Participate in on-call rotation with support from senior engineers; help investigate and resolve infrastructure incidents
Contribute to monitoring dashboards and alert configuration across hybrid environments
Collaboration
Work closely with senior engineers and application teams to understand infrastructure needs and translate them into tickets and tasks
Keep runbooks, wikis, and operational documentation current as you learn systems
Flag issues, ambiguities, and potential improvements — your observations from ground-level operations matter
Requirements
3–5 years of experience in infrastructure, DevOps, platform engineering, systems administration, or a related role
At least one full-time industry role beyond your first job (internships and co-ops count toward the foundation, but we're looking for professional experience in a production environment)
Comfortable with Linux system administration: file systems, networking, process management, bash scripting
Hands-on experience with at least one IaC tool — Terraform or Ansible preferred
Working knowledge of AWS fundamentals: EC2, VPC, IAM, S3, and basic networking concepts
Basic networking understanding: IP addressing, DNS, VLANs, firewalls — you don't need to configure BGP from scratch, but you should be able to troubleshoot a connectivity issue
Experience with or exposure to Kubernetes — doesn't need to be bare metal, but you should understand the basics of pods, deployments, and services
Scripting ability in Python or Bash for automation tasks
Nice to Have
Any exposure to physical infrastructure: data center work, homelab, or on-prem environments in a professional setting
Familiarity with configuration management tools (Ansible, Salt, or similar)
AWS certification (any level) or in-progress certification
Experience with observability tooling: Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, or ELK
